player.speaker: Front Commissar
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.reaction-briliant.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.reaction-briliant.text: The Tisza crossing succeeded. I will not pretend the staff expected it - the Romanian command certainly did not.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.reaction-tactical.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.reaction-tactical.text: The offensive has broken on the far bank. What remains is to decide where this army makes its last stand.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.reaction-victory.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.reaction-victory.text: We hold a bridgehead. Whether it can be supplied across a river under observed artillery is the only question that now matters.
line.extra-alternate-history.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.extra-alternate-history.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.extra-alternate-history.text: Paris expected the northern army to dissolve after the evacuation. Bucharest expected the Tisza to be the end of us. Neither expectation has yet become a fact; what remains is an army, a government, and very little time.
line.callback-advance-deep.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.callback-advance-deep.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-advance-deep.text: The offensive reached further than Szolnok, further than the staff plan, further than the Romanian command believed possible. Whatever happens on this bank, that happened.
line.callback-bridgehead-only.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.callback-bridgehead-only.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-bridgehead-only.text: We hold a bridgehead and no more. The crossing succeeded; the exploitation did not.
line.callback-committed-deep.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.callback-committed-deep.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-committed-deep.text: We committed the reserve deep, as you ordered. There is nothing left behind the line to commit again.
line.callback-held-central.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.callback-held-central.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-held-central.text: You held the reserve centrally, and it remains the one formation on this map not committed to a collapsing report. Landler wanted it across the river sooner. Today he wants to know whether preserving it was foresight—or merely postponing the order it must now receive.
line.telephone-lines-fail.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.telephone-lines-fail.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.telephone-lines-fail.text: The field telephones east of the Tisza are going silent one by one. Some lines have been cut by shellfire; others end at headquarters that have already moved. On the map the bridgehead is still a coloured shape. On the roads it is columns searching for orders.
line.julier-opening.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.julier-opening.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.julier-opening.text: The advance has stopped. Divisions east of Szolnok are exhausted, ammunition crosses the river slower than casualties return, and Romanian formations are concentrating for a counterattack. Whatever surprise existed is gone; what remains is command, bridges and the discipline to choose what can still be held.
line.landler-question.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-question.text: Reports say the enemy knew our axes of advance. Whether through reconnaissance, intercepted orders or betrayal no longer matters. The question is visible from every road: do we hold the eastern bridgehead with the last reserve, or begin a phased withdrawal while the crossings still belong to us?
line.landler-question.choice.hold-east-b: Hold the eastern bridgehead with every available reserve and deny the enemy the initiative.
Gain a larger prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo the withdrawal's full resupply.
line.landler-question.choice.phased-with: Withdraw the most exhausted units first and build a final defence around the crossings on the west bank.
Fully resupply every core formation and gain a smaller prestige award, but forgo the final stand's core-wide experience.
line.julier-hold.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.julier-hold.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.julier-hold.text: Then shorten the perimeter and mass the guns. Do not defend empty ground. The bridgehead survives only if its flanks and the bridge itself remain under one command.
line.landler-hold-warning.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-hold-warning.text: I asked for a decision and you have given one. Do not mistake refusal to yield for a plan, Commissar. If the bridgehead cannot feed itself, courage will consume the last reserve exactly as retreat would have surrendered the ground.
line.landler-withdraw.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-withdraw.text: A withdrawal may save the army, but it must begin before the enemy reaches the bridges. Mark the order of movement now and leave disciplined rear guards, not abandoned battalions.
line.julier-withdraw-warning.speaker: Ferenc Julier
line.julier-withdraw-warning.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.julier-withdraw-warning.text: And understand what the order will sound like east of the river: after Slovakia, another withdrawal promised as preservation. If the first regiment believes the government has abandoned the bridgehead, no timetable will prevent the fifth from calling it a rout.
line.kun-crisis.speaker: Béla Kun
line.kun-crisis.text: Each dead telephone reaches Budapest as a new rumour. Foreign missions wait for the government to fall; our enemies wait for the army to vanish. Preserve enough organised force that the first troops into the capital do not dictate everything that follows.
line.landler-final.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-final.text: Those three points keep the bridges and guns under one command. Hold them while the fresh Romanian formations arrive. Counterattack only where success repairs the line—not where pride asks for another grave.
epilogue.east-bank-victory.speaker: Ferenc Julier
epilogue.east-bank-victory.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
epilogue.east-bank-victory.text: The bridgehead held, and for several days formations still moved by orders instead of rumours. It did not save the Republic. Landler calls the stand proof that the army's spirit survived. I count the reserves and guns it spent.
epilogue.east-bank-defeat.speaker: Jenő Landler
epilogue.east-bank-defeat.text: The last reserve died east of the river with the bridgehead. No organised force remained here to cover the fugitives. As counterrevolutionary vengeance hardens into the White Terror, survivors will ask why command spent their comrades after the position was lost.
epilogue.west-bank-victory.speaker: Béla Kun
epilogue.west-bank-victory.text: The army surrendered the bridgehead and crossed in order. It could not keep the Governing Council in power; after 1 August those battalions defended no state. They could still escort threatened comrades, hide weapons and deny the counterrevolution an entirely helpless enemy.
epilogue.west-bank-defeat.speaker: Ferenc Julier
epilogue.west-bank-defeat.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
epilogue.west-bank-defeat.text: The withdrawal began too late. Scattered battalions reached the west bank, but no headquarters could assemble them. As the White Terror begins settling political accounts, those fragments may still hide or escort a few comrades. They can no longer protect the state.
